verses.restored: Man of Ephraim was called together and crossed northward. They said to Jephthah, Why did you cross to fight against sons of Ammon and not call us to go with you? Your house we will burn over you with fire.

familiar.text: And the men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and went northward, and said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thine house upon thee with fire.

modern.text: Then the men of Ephraim assembled and crossed the Jordan to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, “Why have you crossed over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down with you inside!”

verses.restored: Jephthah said to them, A man of great conflict I was, I and my people, with sons of Ammon. I cried out to you, but you did not save me from their hand.

familiar.text: And Jephthah said unto them, I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, ye delivered me not out of their hands.

modern.text: But Jephthah replied, “My people and I had a serious conflict with the Ammonites, and when I called, you did not save me out of their hands.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִפְתָּח֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֣ישׁ רִ֗יב הָיִ֛יתִי אֲנִ֛י וְעַמִּ֥י וּבְנֵֽי עַמּ֖וֹן מְאֹ֑ד וָאֶזְעַ֣ק אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא הוֹשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם אוֹתִ֖י מִיָּדָֽם

verses.restored: I saw that you were not a savior, so I placed my life in my palm and crossed toward sons of Ammon, and YHWH gave them into my hand. Why have you come up to me this day to fight against me?

familiar.text: And when I saw that ye delivered me not, I put my life in my hands, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and the LORD delivered them into my hand: wherefore then are ye come up unto me this day, to fight against me?

modern.text: When I saw that you would not save me, I risked my life and crossed over to the Ammonites, and the LORD delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come today to fight against me?”

familiar.text: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought with Ephraim: and the men of Gilead smote Ephraim, because they said, Ye Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim among the Ephraimites, and among the Manassites.

modern.text: Jephthah then gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. And the men of Gilead struck them down because the Ephraimites had said, “You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim, living in the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.”

modern.text: The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim, and whenever a fugitive from Ephraim would say, “Let me cross over,” the Gileadites would ask him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he answered, “No,”

modern.text: they told him, “Please say Shibboleth.” If he said, “Sibboleth,” because he could not pronounce it correctly, they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. So at that time 42,000 Ephraimites were killed.

translation_notes: Ephraim begins with a threat to burn Jephthah's house over him, echoing the fire threat used against Samson's wife. The threat is domestic terror, not legitimate accountability.
Unlike Gideon in Judges 8, Jephthah does not de-escalate Ephraim's grievance; wounded honor rapidly becomes Israelite civil war.
The insult in verse 4 attacks Gileadite belonging and treats them as displaced leftovers within Ephraim and Manasseh. The narrative exposes identity contempt as fuel for mass violence.

Shibboleth means an ear of grain or a stream/flood, but here pronunciation becomes an identity checkpoint. Accent or speech difference is not moral evidence and must never justify exclusion, detention, deportation, or killing.
The verb in verse 6 is slaughter, and the forty-two-thousand figure may be stylized, inflated, or textually difficult. Whatever its scale, the scene is a massacre at an escape route.
Jephthah's six-year judgeship is reported without praise and follows the destruction of his daughter and fellow Israelites.
Verse 7's burial phrase is plural, 'in cities of Gilead,' though many translations smooth it to one city; it remains an audit point.
Ibzan's exchange of daughters and daughters-in-law likely reflects household alliance and status networks. Women are not commodities, diplomacy instruments, or proof of a leader's greatness.
Elon receives only a brief tenure and burial notice.
Abdon's seventy donkey riders signal wealth, mobility, and an extended elite household. Family size and status display are not measures of moral worth.
safety_note: Do not use Shibboleth as a romantic symbol of clever security, righteous border control, or cultural purity. It is a lethal language test used against fleeing kin. Reject accent discrimination, tribal essentialism, collective blame, arson threats, civil-war triumphalism, and the treatment of women or descendants as status assets.
